title: Paper Shape Chain · Together
hook: Find a game, gather your friends and start playing.

knows: The group wants an activity to play together.
doesNotKnow: The setup, turn and ending for this house-rule format.

misconception: The group has to know a complicated rulebook before starting.
objective: Learn how to play Paper Shape Chain · Together with friends.

claims.text: Original house rules: Choose three simple shapes, such as a circle, triangle and square. The lead draws a connected chain containing each chosen shape exactly once. All three shapes appear once and touch the next shape in the chain. Play eight turns in total, rotating the lead. The group wins together if at least five turns succeed.
claims.source: Original playable house-rule proposal; not an authoritative ruleset for a traditional game.

claims.text: For this version: 2–8 players; materials: Paper and pencil.
claims.source: Proposed setup and player range for this activity.

recall.question: In Paper Shape Chain, what counts as a successful turn?
options: All three shapes appear once and touch the next shape in the chain.
The lead skips the turn without attempting it.
The group ends the round before anyone plays.
recall.why: All three shapes appear once and touch the next shape in the chain.
